learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Amygdala.
Explain how the Amygdala contributes to distributed brain function.
Connect Amygdala physiology with clinically relevant symptoms and conditions.
Interpret structural or functional findings cautiously and in context.

anatomy.label: Lateral nucleus
anatomy.detail: Receives converging sensory information and learns cue associations.
anatomy.clinical: Supports conditioned responses to predictive cues.

anatomy.label: Basal nuclei
anatomy.detail: Integrates hippocampal and prefrontal information with learned value.
anatomy.clinical: Helps distinguish safe from dangerous contexts.

anatomy.label: Central nucleus
anatomy.detail: Projects to hypothalamic and brainstem systems controlling autonomic and defensive responses.
anatomy.clinical: Excess output can amplify arousal and avoidance.

anatomy.label: Intercalated cells
anatomy.detail: GABAergic clusters regulate flow from basolateral to central nuclei.
anatomy.clinical: Important for extinction and flexible inhibition.

anatomy.label: Extended amygdala
anatomy.detail: Includes bed nucleus pathways involved in prolonged apprehension.
anatomy.clinical: Distinguishes sustained anxiety from brief phasic fear.
